verdict.statement: Fit to freeze as the final Phase 1 source dataset. All automated checks pass, 4 genuine inconsistencies found in this pass were corrected with a deterministic regeneration that changed only 4 interactions, and no confirmed inconsistency remains open. The items listed under human_review_required are recommended confirmations, not blockers.

new_fact_trace.fact: Ethan has an existing college account of about $85k
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: David started a college account when Ethan was born. There's about eighty-five in it. The rest comes out of income. I don't want Ethan choosing a school on price.
new_fact_trace.notes: Single mention; Ethan is 17 (profile) and applying this autumn; nothing contradicts it.

new_fact_trace.fact: Walk-away price of $22M against the $24M letter of intent
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Twenty-two. Below twenty-two I walk.
new_fact_trace.notes: Arithmetic checked: 2M price drop x ~0.6 after tax = 1.2M; 13.5M cash at closing (INT-058) -> 12.3M as stated in INT-077. Recorded as a floor 'where I am today', not a decision, and not restated after the INT-083 decision to sell; no contradiction.

new_fact_trace.fact: Retention pool of up to ~$1.2M, ~$700k after tax
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Out of your proceeds, you mean. After tax that's roughly seven hundred thousand less in your pocket. Can you live with that?
new_fact_trace.notes: Tentative idea, never decided; stays tentative in the manifest. The 700k after-tax cost implies roughly a 40% tax effect, stated by the advisor as 'roughly'.

new_fact_trace.fact: $55k pre-signing costs ($40k retainer + $15k advance) paid from cash
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Fifty-five thousand out of your own pocket before the deal pays for itself. Where's it coming from?
new_fact_trace.notes: 40k + 15k = 55k. Cash 220k -> 165k afterwards; no later meeting quotes a Rebecca cash balance, so nothing contradicts the new level.

new_fact_trace.fact: 12-month paid consulting role after closing (corrects 'salary stops at closing')
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: No, and I should have said so. The draft keeps me on as a paid consultant for twelve months after closing, at my current salary. Lakeshore wants me for the handover. It's in section six.
new_fact_trace.notes: The earlier assumption is preserved in INT-130 (advisor says income stops at closing) and explicitly superseded in INT-142 (later). Correction wording attributes the error to the advisor's assumption.

new_fact_trace.fact: Lucia born Tuesday 3 March; the 4 March meeting is a call from hospital
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Lucia was born on Tuesday, March 3. Mother and baby are doing well, and yes, I'm still in the hospital. I didn't want to cancel
new_fact_trace.notes: INT-045 (2 March) has her at 39 weeks, 'any day now'; January said baby due in March; 5 weeks later (10 April) Lucia smiles for the first time. Token date resolves to Tuesday, March 3 (a Tuesday).

new_fact_trace.fact: Manager hinted at a four-day week (about -20% salary)
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Good. You also mentioned your manager might let you move to four days after leave?
new_fact_trace.notes: Tentative in INT-045; closed as 'not now' in INT-147; no intermediate contradiction.

new_fact_trace.fact: Sofia's student loans are federal
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Federal. And what's an elimination period? The broker used that on the disability quote and I nodded like I knew.
new_fact_trace.notes: INT-019 gives $48k at 5.2% without a type; nothing contradicts federal.

new_fact_trace.fact: Survivor pension is 60% of Samuel's pension (corrects 'about half')
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: More. The form says sixty percent for life, or a lump-sum alternative that we haven't evaluated yet. I had read the company's summary too loosely.
new_fact_trace.notes: Original 'about half' statement is in INT-029 (9 Feb); INT-050 (9 Mar) explicitly corrects it and keeps the original. No later mention uses 'half' for Grace.

new_fact_trace.fact: First investing step on 1 June of ~$24k (one of six)
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: It isn't silly. Let me be concrete. The first step is one sixth of the amount heading into stocks, about twenty-four thousand dollars. If that fell twenty percent, you'd be down about forty-eight hundred.
new_fact_trace.notes: Arithmetic: 6 x 24k = 144k = 10 points of $1.45M, i.e. 15% -> 25% as agreed in INT-097; a 20% fall of 24k = 4.8k as stated. INT-097 says only 'starting next month'; the date 1 June (a Monday) first appears in INT-110 and is confirmed by the advisor. v1 had the investing-step meetings dated before this; fixed in revision 2.

new_fact_trace.fact: Annual house cost of 'fifteen thousand or more'
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: So fifteen thousand or more. But I'd rather you not decide this in the first year. In January you said no large irreversible decisions fo
new_fact_trace.notes: Client states property tax ~9k and insurance 2k (=11k) plus unquantified upkeep; the 15k is the advisor's estimate. Not contradicted anywhere.

new_fact_trace.fact: April tax shortfall of $20-25k, covered ~22k from invoices and ~3k from cash
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: twenty-seven thousand, plus federal income tax, plus state. I'd expect fifty-five to sixty all in. So you're short by twenty to twenty-five, due in April.
new_fact_trace.notes: Feb 25 -> Apr 15 is seven weeks as stated. INT-076 closes the loop (22k of 25k from invoices, rest from cash). Estimates paid for 2025 (35k) were his own guess (INT-016), consistent with the shortfall being on the 2025 return.

new_fact_trace.fact: Estimated taxes use the safe-harbor method (110% of last year's tax)
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Then we can't be precise today. There's a safe harbor: if you pay at least a hundred and ten percent of last year's total tax, in four equal installments, there's no underpayment penalty however big this year turns out.
new_fact_trace.notes: Decided INT-016, applied INT-118; 110% applies because net income (~190k) exceeds the 150k threshold.

new_fact_trace.fact: Remaining Vantora position about a sixth of liquid assets after three sales
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Good question. After the three sales it's down to roughly a sixth of the liquid portfolio, and you've chosen to hold the rest until after the third-quarter earnings.
new_fact_trace.notes: v2 text said 'a fifth' and cited the hold-until-Q3 decision on 29 May, eleven days before it was made (9 June). Arithmetic: ~33% start, -30% fall, 40% trimmed => ~14-17%. Text is now step-aware: starting-size wording until the third sale, 'about a sixth' only after it.

new_fact_trace.fact: Required distribution about $31k; $6k of it via the church gift
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Dennis Hall has confirmed the numbers for the church gift. Your required distribution this year is about thirty-one thousand. A qualified charitable distribution of six thousand counts toward it, and it isn't added to your taxable inc
new_fact_trace.notes: 31k - 6k = 25k as stated in INT-129. No IRA balance appears in any dialogue, so 31k cannot be tied to a balance; plausible for age 74 with a ~0.8M IRA.

new_fact_trace.fact: Aide five days a week at ~$6,400 a month; spending $10,100; portfolio gap $3,800
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: No, it's five days now. Since Frank's fall in March the agency moved us up, and the invoice for May was sixty-four hundred.
new_fact_trace.notes: 5,200 -> 6,400 is +1,200 and 8,900 -> 10,100 as stated. But the gap was given as 4,200 (and 3,000 in INT-009) while January's own figures give 8,900 - 6,300 = 2,600, so the new gap is 10,100 - 6,300 = 3,800. INT-009 and INT-119 corrected; the January statements are untouched.

new_fact_trace.fact: Remaining required amount taken monthly Jul-Dec with 12% withheld
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Dennis said twelve percent. Is that what you want?
new_fact_trace.notes: The 12% is attributed to the accountant Dennis, who is mentioned earlier (INT-028, INT-085), but 12% appears first in the advisor's own turn in INT-129. Not contradicted. Left as is: it is the advisor reporting an accountant's figure.

new_fact_trace.fact: Maturing bond rung of about $50k
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: No, the opposite. The bond pays back its face value in cash, about fifty thousand dollars. The question is what to do with the cash.
new_fact_trace.notes: At the corrected 3,800 a month, one year of withdrawals is ~46k, so a ~50k rung fits. No earlier statement gives a rung size.

new_fact_trace.fact: Frank's pension survivor amount unconfirmed (carried forward)
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: That's worth knowing, and it affects how much you can safely spend. For now I'll record that the survivor amount is unconfirmed, and we'll come back to it when we look at the care costs.
new_fact_trace.notes: INT-009 promised to return to it 'when we look at the care costs'; INT-041 and INT-119 did not. INT-119 now carries it forward as still unconfirmed with Peg's own estimate of about half used for the stress case. No answer is invented.

new_fact_trace.fact: Working assumption of six months' base salary as severance
new_fact_trace.speaker: Advisor
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: That's a reasonable instinct. I'll use a conservative working assumption of six months of base salary and replace it if you ever learn the real terms. On that basis, cash plus severance would cover well over a y
new_fact_trace.notes: 'Well over a year' of cover depends on a base salary that is not stated in any dialogue; with 150k cash alone ~13 months, the claim holds for any plausible salary. Not contradicted.

new_fact_trace.fact: Ren's 14k is the program fee, flights and housing, not extra tuition
new_fact_trace.speaker: Client
new_fact_trace.supporting_dialogue: Ren wants to spend a semester in Seoul next spring. The program would cost about fourteen thousand beyond normal tuition.
new_fact_trace.notes: INT-091 (client: 'beyond normal tuition') -> INT-114 (advisor note had it as extra tuition; client corrects). Original statements preserved.
